A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same SlideAgent paper with 24 complete pages, including Appendices A–F. Full text and rendered-page comparisons establish that the research content matches; differences are confined to the first-page arXiv stamp and administrative metadata.

before.justification: v3.pdf reports original question-answering and retrieval experiments, ablations, error analysis, and computational-cost measurements in Section 3 and Appendix D.

after.justification: v4.pdf retains the same original empirical results in Section 3 and Appendix D, including benchmark comparisons and component ablations.

M1.justification: Section 2 and Appendix B retain identical hierarchical agents, knowledge refinement, element merging, query routing, retrieval, and answer synthesis procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same coverage: SlideVQA, TechSlides, FinSlides, InfoVQA, and the DocVQA experiment in Appendix D.3. No dataset, task, domain, or test scenario changes.

E2.justification: Comparator membership matches in every corresponding experiment, including the multimodal LLM and RAG/agentic comparisons in the tables and the MDocAgent comparison in Figure 3.

E3.justification: The retrieved-page and ground-truth-page settings, backbone configurations, answer normalization, evaluation metrics, and 40-case error-analysis sample are unchanged.

E4.justification: Both versions contain the same error analysis, retrieval analysis, agent/subquery ablations, and qualitative examples in Figures 5–9, together with the same computational-cost analysis in Appendix D.4.

E5.justification: Uncertainty reporting is identical, including the ± quantities in Table 8 and Appendix D.4. No repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, or statistical testing procedures are added or revised.

E6.justification: All numerical entries, plotted results, and qualitative findings match. For example, both versions report SlideAgent/GPT-4o overall scores of 84.9/77.0 on SlideVQA in Table 2 and 94.5/93.6 on DocVQA in Table 7.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulations in Section 2 and Appendix B, including Equations 1–5 and the bounding-box merging construction, are identical. No assumptions, proofs, or derivations change.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same hierarchical document-understanding contribution and performance claims, including the stated +7.9% proprietary-model and +9.8% open-source-model improvements.

C2.justification: Interpretations of retrieval gains, agent ablations, failure categories, and amortized costs are unchanged. Section 6 retains the same limitations concerning element-boundary variation and the primary reliance on textual retrieval.

D1.justification: Implementation parameters, tools, computational-cost disclosures, model specifications, prompt templates, and code/data access information are identical. The PDF license metadata changes from CC BY 4.0 to CC BY-SA 4.0 for the article itself; no change to experimental-resource access is reported.

R1.justification: Section 4, Appendix A, and the reference list are identical. No cited works or substantive positioning relative to prior research change.

P1.justification: The first-page margin stamp changes from arXiv v3 dated 23 April 2026 to v4 dated 5 June 2026. The paper's prose, terminology, headings, and section organization are otherwise identical.

P2.justification: All figures, tables, captions, and their placement are unchanged. Rendered pages 2–24 are pixel-identical, and page 1 differs only in the version/date stamp, without changing the paper's layout.

improvement.justification: The scientific content, supporting evidence, reproducibility information, limitations, and presentation remain identical throughout the main text and appendices. The updated arXiv stamp and article-license metadata do not establish a meaningful improvement or deterioration in paper quality.
